This is Cascade Legal Rights Project. The moderator invited us to respond in this thread, and we're glad to.

First, we understand why people are upset. Getting a letter from a law firm right after you've asked for help is scary, and wanting to warn your neighbors makes sense. Nobody was wrong to raise this.

We want to be clear about what happens to the information people give us at a clinic. Our policy prohibits sharing, selling or disclosing attendee information, and it specifically bars giving it to landlords or their attorneys. Sign-in records stay inside our organization and are kept in locked storage.

As for the letters, eviction cases filed in magistrate court are public records. Some law firms use those filings to send mailings to the tenants named in them. That is the likely explanation for the letters described here.

We don't discuss any individual's situation on a public board, so we won't be responding to specific cases in this thread. If you came to one of our clinics and have questions about your own information, please contact us directly at clinic@cascaderights.example or call our office at 404-555-0187. We will talk it through with you.

The clinic is still happening this Saturday, November 14, from 10am to 1pm, and everyone is still welcome. There is one change. The library meeting room is closed that day, so we have moved to the Mt. Zion fellowship hall in East Atlanta. The time is the same, and the side entrance by the parking lot is accessible.

If you have questions about any of this, the email and phone number above are the best way to reach us.
